about.title: Westminster Medical Malpractice Claims
about.longDescription: A hospital stay or clinic visit is supposed to make things better. When it doesn't — because a diagnosis was missed, a medication was mixed up, or a surgeon hurried through a step — the people of Westminster are left sorting out what happened and who answers for it. California's MICRA rules give you one year from the date you discovered the harm to file, and never more than three years from the injury itself. Before a lawsuit, a 90-day notice has to go to the provider. And a doctor's opinion is nearly always needed to show that care fell below the accepted standard, because a disappointing result on its own is not malpractice. Westminster residents, roughly 92,000 across this Orange County city, receive care at a range of hospitals, urgent-care clinics, and specialty practices in and around town. We handle medical malpractice cases on contingency, meaning no fee unless there is a recovery.

items.title: The clock is shorter than people expect
items.desc: MICRA generally allows one year from discovery and no more than three years from the injury. We can pin down which date applies to you before the window closes.

items.title: The 90-day notice is handled correctly
items.desc: California requires notice to the provider before a malpractice suit is filed. Our team knows this step and builds it into the timeline from the start.

items.title: Expert review comes first, not last
items.desc: A qualified medical expert is almost always needed to show the standard of care was breached, and non-economic damages are capped at an amount that rises each year. We evaluate both early so you know what you are dealing with.

items.question: I was treated after a collision on Beach Boulevard and the ER missed a fracture. Is that malpractice?
items.answer: It might be, but only if a reasonably careful emergency physician would have caught the fracture under the same circumstances. Westminster saw 112 people injured in traffic collisions in 2025, and many of them passed through local emergency rooms, so this scenario is not unusual. We typically have a medical expert review your imaging and chart before deciding whether a claim is viable.

items.question: My surgery didn't go the way I hoped. Do I have a case?
items.answer: Not necessarily. Under California law, a poor result on its own is not malpractice; there has to be a departure from accepted medical practice that caused the harm. We can review your records and tell you honestly whether that line was crossed.

items.question: Do you charge me anything, and will you be handling the case?
items.answer: We handle malpractice matters on contingency, meaning there is no fee unless there is a recovery. Contact us today for a free consultation to discuss your case.
